Chest (mechanical engineering).question: The _____ was Combustion engine component.
Chest (mechanical engineering).fact: A valve chest (often called a steam chest) is a chamber or housing in a steam engine that contains valves controlling the admission, distribution, or regulation of steam. In reciprocating steam engines, the valve chest is typically mounted adjacent to or above the cylinder and encloses the valve gear that distributes steam during operation.

Combustion chamber.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Combustion chamber.question: The _____ was Part of an internal combustion engine or steam engine.
Combustion chamber.fact: A combustion chamber is part of an internal combustion engine in which the fuel/air mix is burned.

Combustion chamber.fact: Most engines use a single spark plug per cylinder, however some (such as the 1986-2009 Alfa Romeo Twin Spark engine) use two spark plugs per cylinder.

Combustion chamber.question: Cannular type: _____ the can type combustor, can annular combustors have discrete combustion zones contained in separate liners with their own fuel injectors
Combustion chamber.fact: Cannular type: Like the can type combustor, can annular combustors have discrete combustion zones contained in separate liners with their own fuel injectors. Unlike the can combustor, all the combustion zones share a common air casing.

Compression ratio.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Compression ratio.question: The _____ was Combustion chamber capacity ratio.
Compression ratio.fact: The compression ratio is the ratio between the maximum and minimum volume during the compression stage of the power cycle in a piston or Wankel engine. The simpler way is the static compression ratio: in a reciprocating engine, this is the ratio of the volume of the cylinder when the piston is at the bottom of its stroke to that volume when the piston is at the top of its stroke.

Compression ratio.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Compression ratio.question: Several production engines have used higher compression ratios, including: Cars built from _____ to 1972 which were designed for high-octane leaded gasoline, which allowed compression ratios up to 13:

Compression ratio.fact: This can also be expressed as a volumetric efficiency of 110%.

Connecting rod.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Connecting rod.question: The _____ was Piston engine component which connects the piston to the crankshaft.
Connecting rod.fact: A connecting rod, also called a 'con rod', is the part of a piston engine which connects the piston to the crankshaft. Together with the crank, the connecting rod converts the reciprocating motion of the piston into the rotation of the crankshaft.

Connecting rod.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Connecting rod.question: The predecessor to the connecting length is the mechanical linkage used by _____-era watermills
Connecting rod.fact: The predecessor to the connecting length is the mechanical linkage used by Roman-era watermills. An early example of this linkage has been found at the late 3rd century Hierapolis sawmill in Roman Asia (modern Turkey) and the 6th century saw mills at Ephesus in Asia Minor (modern Turkey) and at Gerasa in Roman Syria.

Connecting rod.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Connecting rod.question: Notable engines to use fork-and-blade rods include the Rolls-_____ V12 aircraft engine, EMD two-stroke Diesel engines, and various Harley Davidson V-twin motorcycle engines

Core plug.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Core plug.question: The _____ was Closure for sand casting core holes on water-cooled internal combustion engine blocks.
Core plug.fact: Core plugs, welch plugs, or freeze plugs are used to fill the sand casting core holes found on water-cooled internal combustion engines. These holes generally have no factory designed purpose after the sand has been removed although some aftermarket temperature sensors may be installed into the location of a core plug on some engine designs.

Core plug.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Core plug.question: When installed by striking the _____ plug with a hammer, the dome collapses slightly, expanding it laterally to seal the hole
Core plug.fact: The Welch plug is dome-shaped and inserted into the casting hole with the convex side facing outwards. When installed by striking the Welch plug with a hammer, the dome collapses slightly, expanding it laterally to seal the hole.

Crankcase.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Crankcase.question: The _____ was Crankshaft housing in reciprocating combustion engines.
Crankcase.fact: A crankcase is the housing in a piston engine that surrounds the crankshaft. In most modern engines, the crankcase is integrated into the engine block.

Airlift pump.fact: An airlift pump is a pump that has low suction and moderate discharge of liquid and entrained solids.

Aquarium filter.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Aquarium filter.question: The _____ was Fish tank water filter.

Aquarium filter.fact: The bacteria that then convert nitrite to nitrate are Nitrospira and Nitrobacter.

Aquarium filter.subject: Farm Machinery & Power

Aquarium filter.fact: This may be a filter wool/plastic grid rolled into a circular shape (DLS or "Double Layer Spiral") or any number of plastic media commonly called Bio Balls.

Aquarium filter.subject: Farm Machinery & Power

Artificial heart.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Artificial heart.question: The _____ was Mechanical device which replaces the heart.
Artificial heart.fact: An artificial heart is a device that replaces the heart. Artificial hearts are typically used as a bridge to heart transplantation, but ongoing research aims to develop a device that could permanently replace the heart when a transplant—whether from a deceased human or, experimentally, from a genetically engineered pig—is unavailable or not viable.

Working fluid.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Working fluid.question: The _____ was Pressurized gas or liquid in a heat engine.
Working fluid.fact: For fluid power, a working fluid is a gas or liquid that primarily transfers force, motion, or mechanical energy. In pneumatics, the working fluid is air or another gas which transfers force between pneumatic components such as compressors, vacuum pumps, pneumatic cylinders, and pneumatic motors.

Working fluid.subject: Farm Machinery & Power
Working fluid.question: Examples without phase change include air or hydrogen in hot air engines such as the _____ engine, air or gases in gas-cycle heat pumps, etc
Working fluid.fact: Examples without phase change include air or hydrogen in hot air engines such as the Stirling engine, air or gases in gas-cycle heat pumps, etc.
